themes_detail.label: Dead Trees Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Dead or dying trees complaints spiked 860% THIS WEEK (6 complaints vs. 0.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks), suggesting rapid environmental degradation or disease outbreak affecting street canopy in Williamsbridge/Baychester.
evidence: 6 dead/dying tree complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.6 average per week (860% spike, z-score: 5.42)
Spike is the most recent signal in dataset, appearing only in current week
Aligns with long-standing CB budget request for Parks equipment maintenance, suggesting chronic underfunding may have allowed disease to spread
reporting_angles: Interview Parks Department about what disease or pest is killing trees—is this a localized outbreak or systemic neglect?
Canvass residents on White Plains Road and other major streets to document visible tree die-off and resident health/safety concerns
Cross-reference with historical Parks maintenance records—has tree care been deferred in this district?

themes_detail.label: Homeless Encampment Surge
themes_detail.summary: Homeless Person Assistance complaints exploded 800% LAST WEEK (9 complaints vs. 1.0 weekly average), indicating either a sudden influx of unhoused individuals or a new visible encampment in the district.
evidence: 9 homeless person assistance complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.0 weekly average (800% spike, highest z-score: 11.31)
Spike is most extreme statistical anomaly in dataset across all categories
No prior pattern suggests this is a new, acute issue rather than chronic homelessness
reporting_angles: Locate and document the encampment(s)—where are unhoused people concentrating and why this neighborhood now?
Interview residents about safety concerns, sanitation issues, and quality-of-life impacts
Contact NYPD, NYC Department of Social Services, and local nonprofits to understand what triggered the surge and what resources exist

themes_detail.label: Dead Animal Accumulation
themes_detail.summary: Dead animal complaints spiked 248% LAST WEEK (10 complaints vs. 2.9 weekly average), suggesting potential disease vector or inadequate animal removal services in Williamsbridge/Baychester.
evidence: 10 dead animal complaints LAST WEEK vs. 2.9 weekly average (248% spike, z-score: 6.11)
Coupled with 860% spike in dead trees THIS WEEK, suggests broader environmental health crisis
Long-standing CB budget request for pest control indicates chronic underfunding may have degraded response capacity
reporting_angles: Document locations and types of dead animals—are they clustered geographically or spread across district?
Interview Parks/Sanitation about response times and whether staffing/resources are adequate
Check if spike correlates with unseasonably warm weather, disease outbreak, or predator activity (e.g., hawks, coyotes)

themes_detail.label: Food Safety Violations Spike
themes_detail.summary: Food establishment complaints surged 471% LAST WEEK (10 complaints vs. 1.8 weekly average), indicating possible foodborne illness cluster or enforcement crackdown on vendors in the district.
evidence: 10 food establishment complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.8 weekly average (471% spike, z-score: 4.16)
Vendor enforcement complaints also spiked 367% TWO WEEKS AGO (7 complaints vs. 1.5 average), suggesting coordinated enforcement or emerging problem with food service sector
Consumer complaints also elevated 140% THREE WEEKS AGO, potential related signal
reporting_angles: Obtain DOHMH inspection records for past 2 weeks—what violations are being cited at restaurants/food carts?
Interview residents about any foodborne illness cases or complaints about vendor hygiene
Determine if spike reflects actual increase in violations or intensified enforcement activity by city agencies

themes_detail.label: Graffiti and Illegal Parking Surge
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints jumped 409% LAST WEEK (7 vs. 1.4 average) and illegal parking complaints rose 37% LAST WEEK (271 vs. 198.1 average), suggesting deteriorating neighborhood conditions and possible gang activity or organized vandalism.
evidence: 7 graffiti complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.4 weekly average (409% spike, z-score: 4.27)
271 illegal parking complaints LAST WEEK vs. 198.1 weekly average (37% spike, z-score: 5.23)
Combined signal suggests both environmental disorder and enforcement challenges
reporting_angles: Photograph and map graffiti locations—is tagging concentrated on specific blocks or buildings, suggesting territorial marking?
Interview NYPD and local precinct about any gang activity or enforcement operations
Survey residents on whether they feel unsafe and whether visible disorder has accelerated recently
